what_this_is: One read assembled from four already-independent systems — Crown (regime/positioning/volatility), the Macro Weather x Crown scenario read, SRM sector grades and Thematic Rotation. Nothing here is a new gate or a new score beyond one thing: whether a sector's or theme's current grade agrees with what the leading scenario implies for it.

read_me_first: A market with no clear breadth lead, with volatility around normal. Best fit: an inflation shock — commodities and rates up together. Leading scenario: DISPERSION_REGIME. Two stories fit the tape about equally. No sector currently has a clear enough macro sensitivity to test against this story.

crown.headline: A market with no clear breadth lead, with volatility around normal. Best fit: an inflation shock — commodities and rates up together.
because: Breadth is going sideways — neither the big names nor the average stock is leading.
Single stocks are moving about as much as the index. The index itself is quiet, with VIX at 15.4, lower than 82% of the past two years.
Option dealers are positioned in a way that amplifies moves — expect bigger swings in both directions than the news deserves.
Trend-following funds are mixed across the 18 markets we track, and none is at an extreme — the positioning is not crowded.
Big speculators are unusually long the dollar, the S&P, gold and 5 others; unusually short natural gas, the Nasdaq, silver and 1 others (CFTC data to 2026-08-18).

2 warning signs lit: breadth is rolling over toward its own average and the crowd is already positioned this way. A further 12 showed up on individual markets. No single one of these is a reason to sell. They matter when several point the same way as the breadth reading.
crown.so_what: Own the average stock, not just the leaders — and collect premium against it. That is the closest fit rather than a clean one — 2 of its conditions are not met. Size at 1.00x your normal risk.
watch_for: If the dollar trades above 99.46 (0.5% away), trend funds start buying.
If the 2-year trades above 103.68 (0.6% away), trend funds start buying.
Watch for single stocks becoming more volatile while the index stays calm. That gap is the earliest warning we get.
This reading would strengthen if TLT flat (roc5 1.49%, roc20 -1.42%) reversed.
This reading would strengthen if UUP down (roc5 -0.5%, roc20 -2.24%) reversed.
crown.note: Written from the numbers on this page every time it runs. When the data changes, this changes with it.

scenario.reading: DISPERSION_REGIME leads but REFLATION is within 12%. Two stories fit the same tape; treat the overlap as the honest read, not the winner.
scenario.note: A score is the SHARE OF CONDITIONS MET, not a probability. Nothing here was fitted or backtested and no base rate was measured. The evidence and the missing-conditions lists carry the value; the number only ranks them.

scenarios.story: A stock-picker's tape. Implied correlation collapses and single-stock vol pulls away from a calm index — the index tells you almost nothing about what the average name is doing.
scenarios.expression: Single-name selection over index exposure. Pairs. Sell index vol / own single-stock vol.

scenarios.story: Growth accelerating and yields rising with it. Cyclicals and small caps lead; duration is the funding source.
scenarios.expression: Cyclicals, financials, small caps, energy. Short duration.

scenarios.story: Commodity-led repricing. Rates and the dollar rise together, which is the combination that hurts everything at once.
scenarios.expression: Real assets, energy, short duration. Multiple compression risk.

scenarios.story: Yields fall without credit breaking. The benign version of lower rates — the one where breadth improves rather than hides.
scenarios.expression: Long duration equity, small caps, breadth trades.

scenarios.story: Growth decelerating. Credit widens, small caps break, and duration bids as a hedge rather than as a rate call.
scenarios.expression: Defensives, quality, long duration. Fade cyclical strength.

scenarios.story: Flight to quality. The dollar and gold bid together while credit gives way, and CORRELATION rises — everything trades as one thing, which is what makes it a liquidity event rather than a rotation.
scenarios.expression: Cut gross. Defined-risk downside. Cash is a position.

scenarios.story: The dollar is the whole story and it is draining everything else — commodities, credit and non-US risk together.
scenarios.expression: US large-cap domestic over international and commodities.
